PullRequest.Title: chat: add customization migration assessment telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Report aggregate customization migration telemetry from the existing migration-hint computation path.

- return bounded category counts with the already-computed migration hint
- emit telemetry in `collectCustomizationMigrationHint`, after a non-cancelled hint is computed
- keep `CustomizationMigrationService` free of telemetry side effects
- avoid separate lifecycle scans and avoid recomputing migrations
- emit only category and count; never customization names, paths, IDs, or content

The prior lifecycle-trigger implementation was removed. This PR intentionally does not introduce a generic severity: if we later need to distinguish customizations that still work through compatibility mapping from ones that stopped working, that should be modeled as a specific migration outcome rather than an ambiguous severity level.

Refs #332990

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- targeted ESLint for changed TypeScript files
- telemetry extractor (`@vscode/telemetry-extractor@1.20.4`)
- focused Chromium browser tests: 8 passing
  - customization migration hint result counts
  - hint gating and aggregate telemetry emission
- `git diff --check`

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent-host chat request with migration hints disabled, dismissed, already shown in once mode, or no migration findings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The gating checks complete before invoking the migration provider. When disabled, dismissed, or already shown, neither the existing migration computation nor the new telemetry loop runs. When computation returns no hint, no telemetry runs.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Chat request count, but all added work is skipped for these gated cases.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No migration work or telemetry is scheduled after the synchronous gate; there is no new concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The persisted per-session shown state and workspace dismissal remain the effective suppression mechanisms. The diff does not change their keys, lifetime, or cold/warm behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the changed loop is dominated by the existing hint and cancellation check after the unchanged early-return gates.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: changed telemetry is unreachable in these cases.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the changed work does not execute.

Scenarios.Scenario: First qualifying agent-host chat request in once mode with one or more migration categories
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat request setup awaits hooks, instructions, and the existing migration-hint computation in parallel. The pre-existing prompt-file listing, source-folder resolution, and MCP support resolution remain on that critical path. After they complete, the diff creates a fixed-size count list and synchronously submits one telemetry event per nonempty category before returning the hint; appender completion is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List prompt customizations and resolve harness source folders and MCP support state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing six prompt-list calls across three concurrently started migration categories, source-folder provider calls per distinct target type, and one MCP support-scope resolution; effective cardinality is unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same migration scans and support resolution ran to construct the hint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing provider promise is awaited as one branch of request-context Promise.all.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit chat.customizationMigrationAssessment through the telemetry appender.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event for each nonempty migration category, bounded at four, once for the qualifying request in this session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No assessment telemetry event was emitted from this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Event preparation and appender invocation are synchronous before the hint promise resolves, but desktop IPC/network delivery and web telemetry delivery are not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Migration file/server inventory controls existing scans, while added projection and telemetry cardinality depend only on nonempty categories and are capped at four regardless of inventory size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hooks, instructions, and migration-hint computation run in Promise.all. The four migration categories also start concurrently. The new bounded telemetry loop is sequential, while IPC/network completion is asynchronous and not awaited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing prompt-service and MCP-provider cache behavior is unchanged. Once the hint is consumed, the session state suppresses later requests; no new cache or retained collection is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; changed lines and telemetry implementation establish the exact fixed allocation and appender count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Appender CPU and IPC latency vary by platform, but the fixed cardinality and non-awaited delivery bound the added request-path cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added work is bounded to four tiny records and non-awaited submissions, while all collection-scale work is pre-existing and not recomputed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent-host chat requests with migration hint mode set to always
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every request performs the pre-existing migration-hint branch alongside hooks and instruction collection. The diff then submits telemetry before returning the hint, but does not await transport completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recompute prompt-file migrations, source folders, and MCP support for each request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per request, with the same existing provider-call cardinality as before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Always mode already recomputed and displayed the migration hint on every request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by request-context collection before agent invocation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit one assessment event per nonempty migration category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most four events per chat request; effective growth is request count times the number of nonempty categories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous sanitization/appender enqueue occurs before request-context collection resolves; transport is asynchronous and unawaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost grows linearly with chat turns but is capped at four telemetry submissions per turn and does not grow with customization inventory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing migration categories run concurrently; telemetry submissions are a bounded sequential loop whose underlying desktop IPC/web telemetry work is asynchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced or defeated. Always mode intentionally bypasses the once-per-session suppression; underlying service caches, if any, are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for event frequency and call path; low evidence of any material user-visible cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Long sessions can accumulate events, but this is an explicit experimental always mode and each submission is small and non-awaited; no evidence indicates meaningful latency, throughput, or memory impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: although the diff adds bounded repeated telemetry, the realistic per-turn cost is too small to establish an actionable performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Direct computation of a customization migration hint
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing migration arrays and unsupported-server count are available, the result now includes category counts.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The new work creates exactly four small objects and filters them; it does not iterate the migration inventories again beyond constant-time array length reads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing four migration computations remain concurrent; the changed count construction is synchronous after completion.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key, invalidation, or lifetime changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material because allocation cardinality is statically bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: fixed-size allocation and filtering are negligible and avoid any additional collection scan.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files. The PR reuses already-computed migration results, adds only constant-size count construction, and emits at most four non-awaited telemetry records per eligible request. Existing filesystem/provider/MCP work is neither added nor increased. No high-confidence actionable performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
